Vehicles Act, Praying To Set Aside The Judgment And
Award Dated 12.03.2013 Passed By The Court Of M.A.C.T
And Ftc-I At Bidar, And Consequently Allow The
Present Appeal Thereby Enhance The Compensation
From Rs.90,000/- To Rs.20,00,000/- In The Interest Of
Justice And Equity.

This Appeal, Coming On For Final Hearing, This
Day, The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
Challenging judgment and award dated 12.03.2013 passed by MACT and Fast Track Court-I, Bidar (for short 'tribunal') in MVC no.511/2010, this appeal is filed.

2. Facts in brief are that in an accident that occurred on 04.03.2010, claimant, a minor by name NC:
2023:KHC-K:7432 Umashree, aged 10 years while walking by side of Bidar - Humanabad road,
sustained grievous injuries when car bearing Reg.No.KA-38/M-1952 came from Bidar side and dashed against her and despite treatment, she did not recover fully and sustained permanent Kumari Umashree D/O Nagshetty vs Divisional Manager, And Anr on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132071484/
2 physical disability.
Claiming compensation, claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act was filed against insurer and owner.
3. On service of notice, claim petition was opposed by respondents denying negligence.
It was also pointed out that while complaint and FIR were registered against one Dr.Dilip Rathod as driver of car, ultimately charge sheet was filed against Kushalappa.
It was submitted that there was enormous delay in seizure of unregistered car on 27.03.2010, nearly 24 days after accident.

4. Based on pleadings, tribunal framed following issues:
i) Whether petitioner proves that on 04.03.2010 at 8.30 a.m. accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of car bearing no.KA- NC: 2023:KHC-K:7432 38/M-1952 by its driver and due to impact she sustained injuries?
ii) Whether R.1 and R.2 prove that R.3 violated policy conditions?
iii) Whether petitioner is entitled to compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

iv) What order?
5. Thereafter, father of claimant was examined as PW.1 and Dr.Rajendra Kothari as PW.2.
Exs.P1 to P13 were marked.
No evidence was led by respondents.

6. On consideration, tribunal answered issue no.1 in negative, issue no.2 in affirmative, issue no.3 partly in affirmative and issue no.4 by allowing claim petition in part holding claimant entitled for compensation of Rs.19,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. from respondent no.3.
Claim petition was dismissed against respondents no.1 and 2 - insurer.
7. Assailing said award, appeal is filed.
Grounds urged in memorandum of appeal are mainly seeking NC: 2023:KHC-K:7432 enhancement of compensation.
There is no specific ground urged challenging dismissal of claim petition against insurer.

In any case, perusal of impugned award especially its finding on issue no.1 would reveal that tribunal, after meticulous examination of evidence on record and finding material discrepancies with regard to vehicle involved in accident,
driver that caused accident and direction in which offending vehicle came and dashed against claimant, held that insurer could not be made liable.
Consequently award was passed against owner.
8. Against said award, owner has not preferred appeal, only claimant is in appeal.

Therefore, point that arises for consideration would be:
"Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation?"

sentences.text: As per medical evidence on record namely, Ex.P.6 - Wound Certificate, Ex.P16 - Disability Certificate, Discharge Card at Ex.P15 and Ex.P17 - Mediscan Report, NC: 2023:KHC-K:7432 claimant is stated to have suffered 60% disability to whole body.

10. Ex.P15 - Discharge Summary would indicate that claimant was bleeding from nose, unconscious,
unable to open eyes and there was flexor response to pain.
Needs assistance of attendant constantly for feeding, clothing, bathing, toileting etc".

NC: 2023:KHC-K:7432 Opinion of Doctor is as under:
"i. Patient had grievous head injury, intracranial injury and periorbital and scalp hematoma injury following accident as found on CT scan.
She was treated conservatively.

sentences.text: Tribunal has disbelieved said evidence on ground that claimant was physically challenged prior to accident and injuries cannot be stated to be as a result of accident.

However, considering treatment taken it awarded Rs.20,000/- towards Pain and Suffering, Rs.10,000/- towards Medical Expenses, Rs.10,000/- towards Conveyance and other Incidental Expenses and Rs.50,000/-
towards Discomfort of Life.

In case of minors, Hon'ble Supreme Court in Master Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Company Limited and Another reported in AIR 2014 SC 736 has evolved a structured formula to award compensation in personal injury claims.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Company Limited and Another reported in AIR 2014 SC 736
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. Though as per medical evidence claimant may have suffered from disability prior to accident, it would be safe to hold that clamant sustained disability of less than 10%.
In that light, she would be entitled to Rs.1,00,000/-, apart from medical and incidental expenses.
14. Thus, total compensation would be Rs.1,20,000/. Point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative.

Consequently, following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part with costs.

(ii) Claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,20,000/- as against Rs.90,000/-
awarded by Tribunal, with interest at 6% p.a. from date of petition till date of deposit.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:7432 (iii) Respondent no.3 - insurer is directed to deposit same within period of six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
(iv) In view of disposal of appeal, IA.no.I/2022 is dismissed as unnecessary.
